findings.description: Fail-fast/non-blocking contention semantics: the real `pt_core::Lock::acquire(&self) -> Result<LockGuard, LockError>` is synchronous and returns immediately — `Err(LockError::Held)` when another holder has it, `Err(LockError::Io)` on an acquisition I/O error — with no blocking wait, no timeout, no retry/backoff loop (confirmed in pt-core/src/lib.rs: 'this trait is fail-or-succeed'; the real richer Held{holder,since} policy lives on runtime's try_acquire, outside this trait). SHEET-PUB-004's text ('shall acquire... before mutating... and release it after') is silent on whether acquisition can be refused vs. must block-until-available. The code+tests (HeldLock returning Err(LockError::Held) synchronously; `republish_under_a_held_lock_writes_nothing`) pin a specific try-lock/refuse policy that the spec text never states. This is the item all three B-runs foreground most heavily (their central event-driven/unwanted-behavior item).

Exact non-destructive-refusal contract on failed acquisition: `republish` returns `RepublishOutcome { published: false, stale_tabs: <the pre-call stale set, byte-for-byte unmodified> }` and makes ZERO calls to `batch_update_view`/`set_tab_order`/`write_stale_banner` for any tab that cycle — pinned by `republish_under_a_held_lock_writes_nothing` (asserts `pub_.client().published(POSITIONS_TAB).is_none()`). SHEET-PUB-004 states only that republish 'never writes concurrently'; it does not specify the return-value shape or that the stale-tab set must come back exactly unchanged on a refused attempt. All three B-runs reconstruct this as a distinct requirement (B1 UB1, B2 SHEET-REPUB-LOCK-04/07, B3 item 2/7).

Acquire-exactly-once-per-call invariant: `republish_acquires_the_lock_before_mutating` asserts `lock.acquire_count() == 1` after a republish spanning tab writes AND the `set_tab_order` reassert — i.e. one critical section covers the whole multi-tab batch, not one acquisition per tab or per API call. SHEET-PUB-004's singular phrasing is compatible with this reading but does not itself pin the exact granularity or assert a specific acquire count; that boundary decision is test-enforced, not spec-stated.

Lock-scope / settle-ordering invariant: the lock guards only the write+tab-order half of the cycle. `republish_then_settle` calls `republish` (acquire→writes→set_tab_order→release) and only THEN calls `read_marks` (unlocked). `every_settle_read_happens_after_all_writes_in_a_cycle` pins a strict call-log invariant — `min(index of any ReadPricePass) > max(index of any BatchUpdate)` — holding even across multiple settle polls (a transient→numeric two-poll script). SHEET-PUB-004 talks only about the write/lock relationship; this precise 'every read strictly after every write, and unlocked' guarantee is additional code-side machinery all three B-runs pulled into their reconstruction (it's the natural complement of 'never writes concurrently,' but the spec text doesn't itself say it).

Per-tab-failure handling is decoupled from the lock (weaker cross-run agreement — mainly B3): a `batch_update_view` failure on one tab does not release/reacquire the lock or abort the remaining sequence — the loop continues to the next tab, flags it stale, best-effort writes a banner (swallowing that failure too), and still attempts `set_tab_order` under the SAME guard; only `published` flips to false. SHEET-PUB-004 says nothing about per-tab failure granularity. B1/B2 mention banner/stale behavior only in passing (not as a distinct numbered requirement of this concern); B3 alone promotes it to its own EARS item (#6/#7), so this specific finding has lower B-run agreement than the four above.

notes: Direction A surfaces no material finding despite being internally very consistent: A1/A2/A3 unanimously invent an async, blocking, indefinite-wait `tokio::sync::Mutex` model (Result-propagating error type that aborts the whole batch on the first tab failure, a `Runtime`-owned single `Arc<Mutex<()>>`, non-reentrancy) that is *structurally opposite* the real implementation (a synchronous, fail-or-succeed, machine-local-lockfile `Lock` trait living in pt-core, shared across store/reports/config/import/sheets-view, explicitly reentrant for the same holder, whose `republish` returns a plain `RepublishOutcome` value rather than a `Result` and keeps processing remaining tabs after a per-tab write failure). Despite this large shape mismatch, none of it traces to explicit SHEET-PUB-004 text — the spec is genuinely silent on blocking-vs-failing acquisition, on error-propagation shape, and on reentrancy, so per the grading rule (unanimous A-side invention with no spec-text basis = assumption artifact, not a finding) none of it counts as an A-direction drift. Every explicit clause of the spec text ('acquire... before mutating,' 'release it after,' 'never writes concurrently with another Sheets-mutating primitive') is honored by the real code. Hence the classification rests entirely on Direction B's well-grounded, test-pinned surplus (try-lock/refuse semantics, the exact refusal-outcome contract, acquire-once, and the strict write-then-read ordering invariant), with no matching A-side finding to pair it with — B-ONLY-DRIFT rather than BD-DRIFT.
